headline: Tripled Treasury buyback pushes 10-year yield to a three-year high
dek: Bessent's bond-buyback move and rising oil prices overshadowed next week's FOMC decision.
body:
The Headline: Treasury's tripled bond buyback sent the 10-year yield to its highest level since November 2023, adding to the case for a hawkish surprise at next week's Fed meeting.

What Happened: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced Wednesday that the department will triple its buyback of 10- to 20-year government debt to $6 billion, up from the $2 billion initially unveiled, in an effort to steady the bond market. The move follows an Aug. 19 pledge to at least double buybacks, and came as oil prices kept climbing toward $100 a barrel.

Market Reaction: The 10-year Treasury yield jumped to 4.857%, its highest since November 2023, while the 2-year yield held near 4.39%. The Dow fell 333 points (-0.6%), the S&P 500 lost 0.4%, and the Nasdaq slid 0.5%.

Why It Matters: Markets now price roughly a 58% chance of a 25-basis-point hike at next week's FOMC meeting, up from about 52% after Friday's strong August jobs report.

Fed Watch Take: If oil keeps climbing toward $100, the inflation argument for a hike gets harder for the committee's doves to wave away.
author: D. Marsh

headline: Yen's climb toward seven-month high pressures Nikkei exporters
dek: Bessent's warning against yen-weakness bets sent the currency higher and knocked exporter stocks even as chip shares held up.
body:
The Nikkei 225 slipped 0.19% Wednesday to close at 65,143, giving back an early gain, while the TOPIX eased 0.09% to 4,046.64. The declines came after the yen strengthened to its highest level in nearly seven months, with USD/JPY falling to around 153.63, after U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said he has "pretty good insight" into the Bank of Japan's intervention actions and warned traders against betting on further yen weakness.

A stronger yen weighs directly on Japan's export-heavy names: Nintendo dropped 4%, Fast Retailing fell 2.7%, Advantest lost 2.8% and Mitsubishi UFJ slid 1.5%. Semiconductor and AI-linked shares offered some offset. Rising oil prices, pushing toward $100 a barrel, added to inflation pressure and kept rate-hike bets alive.

Traders are watching the BOJ's next policy meeting, where hawkish signals from advisers close to Prime Minister Takaichi and the fastest wage growth since 1997 have fueled speculation of a September hike.
author: S. Okafor

headline: TAIEX edges higher as TSMC profit-taking caps early rally
dek: Shares gave back early gains as investors turned cautious on TSMC ahead of this week's U.S. inflation data.
body:
The TAIEX closed up 77.58 points, or 0.16%, at 47,183.36 on Wednesday after swinging between 47,060.78 and 47,548.26. TSMC, which accounts for more than 40% of the index's total value, fell 0.20% to NT$2,465.00, down from an intraday high of NT$2,490.00, as investors booked profits after its American depositary receipts had jumped 2.35% overnight.

Momentum stalled as the index approached its June intraday record of 48,218, with dealers citing caution ahead of this week's U.S. consumer price index release. TSMC's supply-chain partners stayed in focus after the company and ASML said they are moving to a larger-format EUV lithography photomask, and after ASML confirmed new tool orders from both TSMC and Samsung tied to AI-driven demand.

Investors are awaiting Taiwan's August export order data, a closely watched read on global chip demand, along with any follow-through from the CPI print's effect on U.S. rate expectations.
author: J. Lindqvist

headline: Vietnam's VN-Index slips as small-caps offset oil-led gains
dek: Early strength from rising oil prices faded as small- and mid-cap declines dragged the benchmark lower.
body:
Vietnam's VN-Index fell 0.18% to close at 1,827.12 points on Wednesday, giving back an early advance built on gains in oil and gas names as global crude prices climbed. Morning leaders GAS (+1.54%) and BSR (+1.30%) faded as profit-taking set in, and the index turned negative in the afternoon on broad weakness in small- and mid-cap stocks, led lower by property majors Vinhomes (VHM, -2.04%) and Vingroup (VIC, -0.76%).

Market breadth was weak, with 190 decliners against 120 advancers. Foreign investors were net sellers of VND 270.8 billion, while turnover rose 2.8% from the prior session to VND 14.6 trillion, suggesting the pullback drew active participation rather than a quiet drift lower.

The index remains up double digits over the past year and close to record territory, so traders will watch whether rising oil prices keep supporting energy names even as the broader market digests recent gains. Vietnam's central bank policy stance, and any follow-through in Fed rate expectations given the dong's sensitivity to U.S. yields, are also on the radar.
author: R. Suarez

headline: AMD jumps 3% as CFO lifts AI chip market forecast to $3 trillion
dek: Chip stocks diverged from a broader tech pullback after AMD's finance chief raised her total addressable market call for AI silicon.
body:
AMD shares rose about 3% Wednesday after CFO Jean Hu said the company's total addressable market forecast for AI chips is trending toward $3 trillion, above the guidance AMD gave when it first outlined the opportunity. Hu said demand signals from anchor customers including Meta, OpenAI and Anthropic have come in above what AMD anticipated when those partnerships were struck. Intel shares also ticked higher on the read-through for foundry and packaging demand.

The move stood apart from a soft broader tape: the Nasdaq Composite slipped as Treasury yields jumped to a three-year high after the U.S. Treasury tripled its bond buyback program. AMD's data center revenue grew 107% year over year last quarter to $6.72 billion, 58% of total sales, underscoring how central AI infrastructure has become to its business. Hu also confirmed TSMC remains AMD's primary wafer supplier.

Watch for confirmation of the higher TAM figure at AMD's next investor update, and Nvidia and Broadcom's upcoming earnings for whether hyperscaler capex guidance keeps climbing alongside it.
author: J. Lindqvist
